claim: The zebrafish retina contains rods and four cone subtypes.
source: The zebrafish retina contains a diverse set of photoreceptor subtypes that is evolutionarily ancient (Baden and Osorio, 2019) and includes rods and four cone subtypes.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text with a citation to Baden and Osorio, 2019.

claim: Rods express rhodopsin (Rho, λmax = 501 nm).
source: rods express rhodopsin (Rho, λmax = 501 nm)
evidence: This is a direct statement about rod opsin expression and spectral sensitivity.

claim: UV cones correspond to short single cones that express an opsin with peak sensitivity at ultraviolet wavelengths (Opn1sw1, λmax = 355 nm).
source: UV cones correspond to the short single cones that express an opsin with peak sensitivity at ultraviolet wavelengths (Opn1sw1, λmax = 355 nm)
evidence: This is a direct statement about UV cone morphology and opsin expression.

claim: S cones correspond to long single cones that express an opsin with peak sensitivity at short wavelengths (Opn1sw2, λmax = 415 nm).
source: S cones correspond to the long single cones that express an opsin with peak sensitivity at short wavelengths (Opn1sw2, λmax = 415 nm)
evidence: This is a direct statement about S cone morphology and opsin expression.

claim: M cones express opsins with peak sensitivities in mid wavelengths (Opn1mw1 - 4, λmax = 467–505 nm).
source: the accessory member corresponds to the M cone, which expresses opsins with peak sensitivities in mid wavelengths (Opn1mw1 - 4, λmax = 467–505 nm)
evidence: This is a direct statement about M cone opsin expression with citation.

claim: L cones express opsins with peak sensitivities at long wavelengths (Opn1lw1 - 2, λmax = 548–558 nm).
source: the principal member corresponds to the L cone which expresses opsins with peak sensitivities at long wavelengths (Opn1lw1 - 2, λmax = 548–558 nm) (Chinen et al., 2003; Endeman et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a direct statement about L cone opsin expression with citations.

claim: Most mammals lost some photoreceptor diversity and only preserved rods and cone subtypes related to the UV and L cones.
source: Most mammals lost some of this diversity, and only preserved rods and cone subtypes related to the UV and L cones (Baden and Osorio, 2019; Musser and Arendt, 2017).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations to support the evolutionary claim.

claim: Photoreceptor subtypes have distinct wiring with retinal circuits.
source: In addition to differences in morphology and opsin expression, photoreceptor subtypes have distinct wiring with retinal circuits (Li et al., 2009; Li et al., 2012)
evidence: This is stated directly with citations.

claim: Photoreceptor subtypes have differences in density.
source: differences in density (Allison et al., 2010)
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: Photoreceptor subtypes have differences in mitochondrial morphology.
source: mitochondrial morphology (Giarmarco et al., 2020)
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: Photoreceptor subtypes are specialized for particular aspects of vision.
source: are specialized for particular aspects of vision (Orger and Baier, 2005; Yoshimatsu et al., 2020; Yoshimatsu et al., 2021)
evidence: This is stated directly with citations.

claim: Differences between photoreceptor subtypes mainly arise from differences in gene expression, ultimately controlled through transcriptional regulation.
source: Such differences mainly arise from differences in gene expression, ultimately controlled through transcriptional regulation (Arendt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: The study generated deep and high-quality transcriptomic profiles (RNA-seq) of the five zebrafish photoreceptor subtypes.
source: First, we obtain deep and high-quality transcriptomic profiles (RNA-seq) of the five zebrafish photoreceptor subtypes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of what the study accomplished.

claim: The study used a CRISPR-based F0-screening approach to test the function of transcription factors.
source: Third, we show that a CRISPR-based F0-screening approach (Hoshijima et al., 2019; Kroll et al., 2021) is a reliable platform to test the function of these transcription factors.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodology used with citations.

claim: F0 larvae that carry mutations in foxq2 lose S cones.
source: F0 larvae that carry mutations in foxq2 lose S cones
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental result.

claim: F0 larvae that carry mutations in nr2e3 lose rods.
source: while those that carry mutations in nr2e3 lose rods (Ogawa et al., 2021b; Xie et al., 2019)
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental result with citations.

claim: The generation of UV cones requires both Tbx2a and Tbx2b.
source: We find that the generation of UV cones requires both Tbx2a and Tbx2b
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental finding.

claim: Tbx2a maintains the identity of L cones by repressing M-opsin expression.
source: Tbx2a and Tbx2b, respectively, maintain the identity of L cones and S cones by repressing M-opsin expression.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental finding.

claim: Tbx2b maintains the identity of S cones by repressing M-opsin expression.
source: Tbx2a and Tbx2b, respectively, maintain the identity of L cones and S cones by repressing M-opsin expression.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental finding.

claim: Manual collection of photoreceptors allowed focusing on fluorescent and healthy photoreceptors with intact outer segments, cell bodies, and mitochondrial bundles.
source: Manual collection allowed us to focus on fluorescent and healthy photoreceptors, with intact outer segments, cell bodies, and mitochondrial bundles, and to avoid cellular debris and other contaminants (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1B showing images of dissociated photoreceptors.

claim: Each RNA-seq sample consisted of a pool of 20 photoreceptors of a single subtype derived from a single adult retina.
source: For each sample, we collected pools of 20 photoreceptors of a single subtype derived from a single adult retina.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methodology.

claim: On average, 86.4% of reads were mapped to the zebrafish genome (GRCz11).
source: On average, we were able to map 86.4% of reads to the zebrafish genome (GRCz11; range: 76.3–90.4%)
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result, also shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The average number of mapped reads per sample was 10.19 million ± 1.77 million.
source: corresponding to 10.19 million±1.77 million mapped reads per sample (mean ± s.d.)
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result, also shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The average number of unique genes per sample was 7936.
source: and to an average of 7936 unique genes per sample (range: 5508–10,420) (Figure 1D)
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result, also shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The manual, cell-type specific, SMART-seq2-based approach provides substantially deeper transcriptomes than single-cell droplet-based techniques.
source: This high quantity of reads and unique genes demonstrates that our technique provides substantially deep transcriptomes — especially when compared to single-cell droplet-based techniques where the number of reads per cell is on average below 20,000, corresponding to more than 2000-fold differences in depth (Hoang et al., 2020; Macosko et al., 2015; Ogawa and Corbo, 2021a).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations and comparison to other methods.

claim: Unsupervised clustering (tSNE) showed that samples correctly clustered by the subtype they were derived from.
source: Using unsupervised clustering (t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding or tSNE), we found that samples correctly clustered by the subtype they were derived from.
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Each sample had high expression of the appropriate opsin and low expression of other opsins.
source: In addition, samples only had high expression of the opsin from the reporter line the sample was derived from and low expression of other opsins, corroborating the purity of our samples (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Principal component analysis revealed that most differences in gene expression were between rods and cones.
source: PCA revealed that most of the differences in gene expression were between rods and cones (Figure 1G, left panel).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Among cones, the biggest differences in gene expression arose from two groupings: UV and S cones vs. M and L cones.
source: When cones were considered separately, the biggest differences in gene expression arose from two groupings: UV and S cones vs. M and L cones.
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: M and L cones showed clear separation in gene expression.
source: Subsequent analysis revealed a clear separation of M and L cones
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: UV and S cones showed the least differences in gene expression.
source: with UV and S cones showing the least differences (Figure 1G)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Differential gene-expression analysis revealed approximately 3000 differentially expressed genes.
source: we performed differential gene-expression analysis by making pairwise comparisons following the directions of the principal components, revealing a diverse set of ~3000 differentially expressed genes, many of unknown function in photoreceptors (Figure 1—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to supplementary data.

claim: The dataset has been made openly available and easy to explore through an online interactive plotter.
source: For this reason, we have made our dataset openly available and easy to explore through an online interactive plotter (https://github.com/angueyraLab/drRNAseq/)
evidence: This is a direct statement about data availability.

claim: The dataset was integrated with other available zebrafish photoreceptor datasets.
source: and integrated it with other available zebrafish photoreceptor datasets (Hoang et al., 2020; Ogawa and Corbo, 2021a; Sun et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations.

claim: 803 transcription factors were detected with significant expression.
source: Therefore, we isolated all RNA-seq reads that could be mapped to transcription factors and detected significant expression of 803 transcription factors.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result.

claim: Neurod1 was the transcription factor with the highest expression by approximately fivefold.
source: When ranked by average expression levels across all samples, neurod1 was revealed as the transcription factor with the highest expression by ~fivefold (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Among the 100 most highly expressed transcription factors, genes well known to be critical during photoreceptor development were identified, including crx, otx5, rx1, rx2, nr2e3, six6b, six7, meis1b, egr1, foxq2, and thrb.
source: Among the 100 most highly expressed transcription factors, we identified genes well known to be critical during photoreceptor development, including crx, otx5, rx1, rx2, nr2e3, six6b, six7, meis1b, egr1, foxq2, and thrb (Figure 2A, blue bars; Furukawa et al., 1997; Shen and Raymond, 2004; Ji et al., 2018; Swaroop et al., 2010; Ogawa et al., 2015; Ogawa et al., 2019; Erickson et al., 2010; Heine et al., 2008; Ogawa et al., 2021b; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: 75 transcription factors showed significant differential expression between rods and cones.
source: By expanding our analysis beyond previously characterized genes, our dataset revealed a total of 75 transcription factors with significant differential expression between rods and cones, many of which have no described function in photoreceptors (Figure 2C and Supplementary Data 2).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to supplementary data and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: 47 transcription factors were differentially expressed between cone subtypes.
source: By analyzing cone subtypes, we found a total of 47 differentially expressed transcription factors.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result.

claim: Seven transcription factors were significantly enriched in both L and M cones compared to UV and S cones.
source: Seven transcription factors were significantly enriched in both L and M cones compared to UV and S cones (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Twelve transcription factors were enriched in L cones.
source: Twelve were enriched in L cones, including thrb — known to be critical to generate L-cones across vertebrates (Ng et al., 2001; Suzuki et al., 2013) — and rxrga — a regulator of L-opsin expression in mouse (Roberts et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations.

claim: Ten transcription factors were enriched in M cones.
source: Amongst the ten M-cone enriched transcription factors, we identified thraa — another thyroid hormone receptor, confirmed to be expressed by photoreceptors (Volkov et al., 2020) — and lrrfip1a.
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: Five transcription factors were enriched in both UV and S cones compared to L and M cones.
source: A small group of just five genes was enriched in both UV and S cones compared to L and M cones and included tbx2b and skor1a.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result.

claim: Seven transcription factors were enriched in S cones, including foxq2.
source: Seven transcription factors were enriched in S cones — including foxq2
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data analysis result.

claim: Two transcription factors were enriched in UV cones: tbx2a and xbp1.
source: and two were enriched in UV cones — tbx2a and xbp1 (Figure 2E and Supplementary Data 3).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to supplementary data and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fluorescent in situ hybridization validated the expression of several transcription factors identified through RNA-seq analysis in photoreceptors.
source: To validate our RNA-seq, we used a fluorescent in situ hybridization assay and detected expression in photoreceptors of several transcription factors identified through this analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Reanalysis of existing RNA-seq datasets confirms that the expression of the identified transcription factors is active during retinal development.
source: Reanalysis of existing RNA-seq datasets confirms that the expression of the identified transcription factors is active during retinal development (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Single-cell zebrafish embryos were injected with Cas9 protein and 2 or 3 guide RNAs (gRNAs) targeting a gene of interest for F0 screening.
source: We injected single-cell zebrafish embryos with Cas9 protein and 2 or 3 guide RNAs (gRNAs) targeting a gene of interest.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methodology.

claim: All guides were tested to ensure a high rate of mutations.
source: All guides were tested to ensure a high rate of mutations (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to Table 2.

claim: Phenotypes were assessed in injected F0 larvae at 5 days post-fertilization (5 dpf).
source: At 5 days post-fertilization (5 dpf) we assessed phenotypes in injected F0 larvae, which are genetic mosaics
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methodology.

claim: All F0 larvae analyses correspond to larvae that have been genotyped to confirm mutations in the targeted gene.
source: All analyses correspond to F0 larvae that have been genotyped to confirm mutations in the targeted gene (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental methodology.

claim: foxq2 is expressed at relatively high levels, ranking 33rd amongst the top enriched transcription factors.
source: Among transcription factors, foxq2 is expressed at relatively high levels, ranking 33rd amongst the top enriched transcription factors (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: foxq2 is specifically enriched in S cones, with negligible expression in other photoreceptor subtypes.
source: It is specifically enriched in S cones, with negligible expression in other photoreceptor subtypes (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Loss-of-function foxq2 mutants are characterized by a complete loss of S cones and S-opsin expression, and a slight increase in M-opsin expression.
source: Loss-of-function of foxq2 mutants are characterized by a complete loss of S cones and S-opsin expression, and a slight increase in M-opsin expression (Ogawa et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: foxq2 F0 mutant larvae displayed a marked decrease of approximately 85% in the density of S cones compared to wild-type controls.
source: Compared to wild-type controls, foxq2 F0 mutant larvae displayed a marked decrease of ~85% in the density of S cones (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: foxq2 F0 mutants showed a small but significant increase of approximately 24% in the density of M cones.
source: Consistent with the slight increase in M-opsin expression reported in germline loss-of-function mutants, we also found a small but significant increase of ~24% in the density of M cones in foxq2 F0 mutants.
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The densities of rods, UV cones, and L cones in foxq2 F0 mutants did not show any significant differences compared to controls.
source: In contrast, the densities of rods, UV cones, and L cones in foxq2 F0 mutants did not show any significant differences (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Quantification of overall cone density did not reveal significant differences in foxq2 F0 mutants compared to control.
source: Quantification of overall cone density — using nuclear staining — did not reveal significant differences in foxq2 F0 mutants compared to control (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: nr2e3 is known to be critical for the generation of rods in vertebrates.
source: As a second positive control, we created mutations in nr2e3 — a rod enriched-gene (Figure 3D), known to be critical for the generation of rods in vertebrates (Cheng et al., 2006; Forrest and Swaroop, 2012; Oh et al., 2008)
evidence: This is stated directly with citations.

claim: nr2e3 F0 mutants have a pronounced loss of approximately 80% of rods.
source: As observed in germline nr2e3 mutants (Xie et al., 2019), nr2e3 F0 mutants have a pronounced loss of ~80% of rods (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation and shown in Figure 3E.

claim: nr2e3 F0 mutants showed an approximately 25% decrease in UV-cone densities.
source: Interestingly, in nr2e3 F0 mutants we also identified a ~25% decrease in UV-cone densities — which has not been previously reported — suggesting an unrecognized role of Nr2e3 in cone development (see discussion) (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The loss of UV cones in nr2e3 F0 mutants is reflected in a decrease in overall cone density.
source: The loss of UV cones is reflected in a decrease in overall cone density in nr2e3 F0 mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The close agreement between germline mutants and foxq2 and nr2e3 F0 mutants demonstrates that the F0 screening approach is reliable.
source: The close agreement between germline mutants and foxq2 and nr2e3 F0 mutants demonstrates that our approach is reliable (phenotypes are clear and quantifiable)
evidence: This is stated directly based on comparison of results.

claim: The F0 screening approach is flexible, as mutations were created using any relevant combination of transgenic lines.
source: flexible (mutations were created using any relevant combination of transgenic lines)
evidence: This is stated directly based on the experimental design.

claim: The F0 screening approach is efficient in terms of cost and labor, as a gene can be evaluated in less than a month by a single person.
source: and efficient in terms of cost and labor (a gene can be evaluated in less than a month by a single person, without significantly increasing burden in animal care).
evidence: This is stated directly based on the experimental experience.

claim: skor1a expression is restricted to UV and S cones across multiple photoreceptor transcriptomic datasets.
source: Across multiple photoreceptor transcriptomic datasets, including ours, the expression of skor1a is restricted to UV and S cones (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, Figure 1—figure supplement 3E)
evidence: This is stated directly with reference to figures.

claim: skor1a expression is high in early stages of cone development.
source: and high in early stages of cone development (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G; Hoang et al., 2020; Ogawa and Corbo, 2021a).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations and reference to a figure.

claim: skor1a F0 mutants have normal UV and S cone densities and normal total cone densities.
source: In disagreement with this hypothesis, we find that skor1a F0 mutants have normal UV and S cone densities and normal total cone densities (Figure 3—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: sall1a F0 mutants have normal rod densities and no disturbance of the cone mosaic or total cone density.
source: Yet, we found that sall1a F0 mutants have normal rod densities and no disturbance of the cone mosaic or total cone density (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: lrrfip1a F0 mutants have normal M-cone densities.
source: Similarly, F0 mutants of the M-cone enriched gene lrrfip1a, have normal M-cone densities (Figure 3—figure supplement 5)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: xbp1 F0 mutants have no appreciable changes in UV-cone or other photoreceptor-subtype densities.
source: and F0 mutants of the UV-cone enriched gene xbp1, have no appreciable changes in UV-cone or other photoreceptor-subtype densities (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: skor1a, sall1a, lrrfip1a, and xbp1 are not critical for the generation of photoreceptor subtypes.
source: These results suggest that these four transcription factors are not critical for the generation of photoreceptor subtypes.
evidence: This is stated directly based on the experimental results.

claim: Tbx2 is known to be differentially expressed in cones of many species, including cichlids, chickens, squirrels, and primates.
source: Tbx2 is known to be differentially expressed in cones of many species, including cichlids (Sandkam et al., 2020), chickens (Yamagata et al., 2021), squirrels (Kunze, 2017), and primates (Peng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated directly with citations.

claim: There are two paralogues of tbx2 in the zebrafish genome: tbx2a and tbx2b.
source: As a teleost duplicated gene, there are two paralogues of tbx2 in the zebrafish genome: tbx2a and tbx2b.
evidence: This is stated directly based on genomic knowledge.

claim: Tbx2b is involved in the determination of UV-cone fate in zebrafish.
source: Work in zebrafish has shown that Tbx2b is involved in the determination of UV-cone fate (Alvarez-Delfin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: Both tbx2a and tbx2b show high expression in UV cones.
source: Our RNA-seq data revealed that both tbx2a and tbx2b show high expression in UV cones (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: tbx2a shows significant enrichment in L cones.
source: In addition, we detected significant enrichment of tbx2a and tbx2b expression in L and S cones, respectively.
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: tbx2b shows significant enrichment in S cones.
source: In addition, we detected significant enrichment of tbx2a and tbx2b expression in L and S cones, respectively.
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: tbx2b F0 mutants had a marked decrease in UV cones (approximately 62%) and an increase in rod density (approximately 3.85-fold).
source: In agreement with previous studies, tbx2b F0 mutants had a marked decrease in UV cones (~62%) and an increase in rod density (~3.85-fold) (Figure 4B and D; Alvarez-Delfin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation and shown in Figure 4B and D.

claim: tbx2a F0 mutants displayed a marked loss of UV cones (approximately 59%) and an increase in rods (approximately 1.86-fold).
source: Surprisingly, we found that tbx2a F0 mutants displayed the same phenotype as tbx2b F0 mutants: a marked loss of UV cones (~59%) and an increase in rods (~1.86-fold) — although the increase in rods was significantly lower in tbx2a F0 mutants than in tbx2b F0 mutants (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The increase in rods was significantly lower in tbx2a F0 mutants than in tbx2b F0 mutants.
source: although the increase in rods was significantly lower in tbx2a F0 mutants than in tbx2b F0 mutants (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Compared to controls, tbx2b F0 mutants have a modest but significant decrease in the sum of rods and UV cones (approximately 14%).
source: Compared to controls, tbx2b F0 mutants have a modest but significant decrease in the sum of rods and UV cones (~14%)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: tbx2a F0 mutants have a marked loss in the sum of rods and UV cones (approximately 39%).
source: and tbx2a F0 mutants have a marked loss (~39%) (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Both tbx2a and tbx2b F0 mutants show a significant decrease in total cone density.
source: As expected, the loss of UV-cone nuclei is readily apparent in both tbx2a and tbx2b F0 mutants (~66.6% and 69.1%, respectively, corresponding to 129 and 134 fewer UV cones than controls), and both mutants show a significant decrease in total cone density (~9.8% and 12.5% respectively, corresponding to 72 and 91 fewer cones than controls) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: tbx2b F0 mutants showed a clear decrease in UV-opsin expression and a significant increase in rhodopsin expression compared to controls.
source: We found that, in comparison to controls, tbx2b F0 mutants showed a clear decrease in UV-opsin expression and a significant increase in rhodopsin expression.
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: tbx2a F0 mutants showed a clear decrease in UV-opsin expression, but without an increase in rhodopsin expression.
source: In comparison, tbx2a F0 mutants also showed a clear decrease in UV-opsin expression, but without an increase in rhodopsin expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both Tbx2a and Tbx2b are required for the generation of zebrafish UV cones.
source: Together our reporter lines and qPCR analyses suggest that, despite 87% protein-sequence similarity and co-expression of the two genes in the same cell, both Tbx2a and Tbx2b are required for the generation of zebrafish UV cones.
evidence: This is stated directly based on the experimental results.

claim: Loss-of-function of either tbx2a or tbx2b leads to a decrease in UV cones and a concomitant routing of photoreceptor progenitors towards a rod fate.
source: Loss-of-function of either gene leads to a decrease in UV cones and a concomitant routing of photoreceptor progenitors towards a rod fate (Alvarez-Delfin et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly with a citation.

claim: In tbx2b F0 mutants routing towards a rod fate appears to be significantly stronger than in tbx2a F0 mutants.
source: In tbx2b F0 mutants routing towards a rod fate appears to be significantly stronger than in tbx2a F0 mutants.
evidence: This is stated directly based on the experimental results.

claim: tbx2a is enriched in L cones, albeit with expression levels lower than in UV cones.
source: In addition to expression in UV cones, we detected significant enrichment of tbx2a in L cones, albeit with expression levels lower than in UV cones (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4A (note: text says 4B but likely refers to 4A).

claim: qPCR quantification revealed a significant increase in M-opsin expression in tbx2a F0 mutants, specifically of opn1mw2.
source: Furthermore, our qPCR quantification of opsins revealed a significant increase in M-opsin expression in tbx2a F0 mutants — specifically of opn1mws2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 (note: text says supplement 1 but likely refers to supplement 2).

claim: In tbx2a F0 mutants, there was a significant but small decrease in the number of L cones (approximately 12%).
source: In tbx2a F0 mutants, we found a significant but small decrease in the number of L cones (~12%) — identified by their tdTomato expression (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In tbx2a F0 mutants, there was a marked increase in the number of GFP-positive cells (presumptive M cones).
source: and a marked increase in the number of GFP-positive cells (presumptive M cones).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In tbx2a F0 mutants, many GFP-positive cells co-express tdTomato (L-cone marker), a phenotype which is not present in control larvae.
source: Interestingly, in tbx2a F0 mutants, many GFP-positive cells co-express tdTomato (L-cone marker) — a phenotype which is not present in control larvae (Figure 5A, middle).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Only a small fraction of L cones is double positive in controls (mean ± s.d.: 5.2%±6.0), but a significantly higher fraction is double positive in tbx2a F0 mutants (mean ± s.d.: 37.5% ± 18.9%).
source: We found that only a small fraction of L cones is double positive in controls (mean ± s.d.: 5.2%±6.0), but a significantly higher fraction is double positive in tbx2a F0 mutants (mean ± s.d.: 37.5% ± 18.9%) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The abnormal expression of GFP in L cones in tbx2a F0 mutants indicates a loss of inhibitory control over the M-opsin promoter.
source: This abnormal expression of GFP in L cones in tbx2a F0 mutants, combined with the increase in M-opsin expression found in our qPCR analysis, indicates a loss of inhibitory control over the M-opsin promoter.
evidence: This is stated directly based on the experimental results.

claim: M cone densities showed no significant changes in tbx2a F0 mutants when double-positive cells were manually excluded.
source: By manually excluding double-positive cells, we counted GFP-only cells to quantify M cone densities and found no significant changes in tbx2a F0 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: tbx2b F0 mutants had a significant increase in the number of GFP-positive cells.
source: While tbx2b F0 mutants also had a significant increase in the number of GFP-positive cells (see next section) (Figure 5A, bottom)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: tbx2b F0 mutants showed no changes in the number of tdTomato-positive L cones.
source: there were no changes in the number of tdTomato-positive L cones (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: tbx2b F0 mutants showed no changes in the percentage of L cones with significant GFP expression (mean ± s.d.: 2.6% ± 1.8%).
source: or in the percentage of L cones with significant GFP expression (mean ± s.d.: 2.6% ± 1.8%%) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated directly and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Tbx2a, but not Tbx2b, is important to preserve L cone identity.
